title: Why else would I?
takeaway: The pain you put up with shows what you really love.
scene: The poet is answering everyone who thinks he's foolish. Each couplet asks 'why else would I…?' as if to say: what I've been through proves how much I love.

original: جے پیار کسے نال ہوندا نہ میں جندڑی رول گواندا کیوں
لوکاں دیاں گلاں کیوں سن دا تھاں تھاں تے بھنڈیا جاندا کیوں
transliteration: Je pyaar kise naal honda na, main jindri rol gaanda kyon
Lokaan diyaan gallaan kyon sun da, thaan thaan te bhandiya jaanda kyon
translation: If I didn't love someone, why would I throw my life away?
Why would I put up with people's talk, and be gossiped about everywhere I go?
couplets.story: If he weren't in love, why would he waste his life like this? Why would he let people talk about him behind his back all over town? He puts up with it because he loves someone.

original: جے محرم راز محبت دا چھڈ راہ دے وچ نہ ٹر جاندا
میں پاسے ہو کے دنیا توں لک لک کے نیر وہاندا کیوں
transliteration: Je mehram raaz mohabbat da chhad raah de vich na tur jaanda
Main paase ho ke duniya ton lukk lukk ke neer vahaanda kyon
translation: If the one who shared love's secret hadn't left me halfway down the road,
why would I step away from the world to cry in hiding?
couplets.story: The one person who knew his heart left him halfway through the journey. That's why he goes off by himself and cries where no one can see.

original: جے عادت اوس شکاری نوں ہوندی نہ دل تڑفاون دی
اوہ ہر پاسے لبھے دوسیاں تے نیناں دے تیر چلاندا کیوں
transliteration: Je aadat os shikaari nu hondi na dil tarfaavan di
Oh har paase labbhe dosiyaan te nainaan de teer chalaanda kyon
translation: If that hunter weren't in the habit of making hearts ache,
why would he aim the arrows of his eyes at everyone he finds?
couplets.story: He calls the beloved a hunter. Hurting hearts must be a habit, he says. Why else would the beloved go around shooting those arrow-like glances at everyone?

original: ہے مڈھوں ریت زمانے دی کوئی وکھرا اوہنے کیتا نئیں
جے پیار نہ ہوندا اک دھوکا اوہ سجن روپ وٹاندا کیوں
transliteration: Hai mudhon reet zamaane di, koi vakhra ohne keeta nahin
Je pyaar na honda ik dhokha, oh sajan roop vataanda kyon
translation: It's been the world's way from the start; he did nothing new.
If love weren't a kind of trick, why would that friend change his face?
couplets.story: He shrugs. This is how the world has always worked, so the beloved isn't special. But if love isn't a trick, why did the person he loved suddenly become someone else?

original: مینوں پاس نہ ہوندا عزت دا، نیناں دے اتھرو نہ رکدے
ایہہ داغ دلے دے زخماں دا لوکاں توں یار لکاندا کیوں
transliteration: Mainu paas na honda izzat da, nainaan de athru na rukde
Eh daagh dile de zakhmaan da lokaan ton yaar lukaanda kyon
translation: If I didn't care about honour, the tears in my eyes would never stop.
Why else, friend, would I hide these scars on my heart from people?
couplets.story: The only thing stopping his tears is his pride. He doesn't want people to know. That's why he hides the scars on his heart.

original: جے دردی ہوندا یار میرا میں زہر پیالے پیندا ناں
اوہ ساقی بن کے غیراں نوں محفل وچ جام پلاندا کیوں
transliteration: Je dardi honda yaar mera, main zehar piaale peenda naa
Oh saaqi ban ke ghairaan nu mehfil vich jaam pilaanda kyon
translation: If my friend had any feeling for me, I wouldn't be drinking cups of poison.
Why would he play saqi and pour for strangers at the gathering?
couplets.story: If the beloved cared at all, the poet wouldn't be swallowing all this bitterness. Instead the beloved is like a host at a party, pouring drinks for everyone else and ignoring him.

original: میرے دل کملے دی مت ماری پیا تڑفے اک نظارے نوں
جیہڑا سفنے دے وچ آندا نئیں او ساہنے مکھ وکھاندا کیوں
transliteration: Mere dil kamle di mat maari, piya tarfe ik nazaare nu
Jehra supne de vich aanda nahin, o saahne mukh vikhaanda kyon
translation: My foolish heart has lost its mind, aching for just one glimpse.
Someone who won't even come to me in dreams, why would he show his face in person?
couplets.story: His silly heart keeps hoping for one look. But the beloved won't even show up in his dreams. Why would they ever appear in real life?

original: احمدؔ ایہہ شعر محبت دے جے دل اوہدے نوں موہ لیندے
کوئی دے کے جام محبت دا اوہ کھوندا تے ترساندا کیوں
transliteration: Ahmad eh shair mohabbat de je dil ohde nu moh lainde
Koi de ke jaam mohabbat da oh khonda te tarsaanda kyon
translation: Ahmad, if these love poems had won his heart,
why would he hand me a cup of love and then snatch it back, leaving me thirsty?
couplets.story: He ends by admitting his poems haven't worked. If they had, the beloved wouldn't keep giving him a taste of love and then taking it away again, leaving him thirsty for more.

deeper: For Sufis, the seeker often feels that God gives a taste of closeness and then withdraws, leaving the soul 'thirsty'. They saw this as a way of deepening longing, not as rejection. The poem's frustration can be read as that stage of the path.
why: It flips the usual question. Instead of 'why do you love?', the poet asks 'why else would I suffer this much?'
prompt: What are you willing to put up with because you care about it?
notes: Couplet 3: 'labbhe dosiyaan' is read loosely as 'everyone he finds'.
